title: Dataset intake validator and prompt versioner for benchmark profile generation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Improve the benchmark harness ingestion and profile publishing pipeline so that model onboarding produces reproducible, audited performance profiles (latency, throughput, quality metrics) while supporting prompt versioning and dataset sampling strategies required for fair comparison across model variants.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: dataset manifest validation, deterministic and stratified sampling, prompt version metadata and diffs, pluggable eval-runner adapter interface, artifact metadata schema for profile publishing.
- Out of scope: rewriting eval metrics themselves or adding new eval tasks beyond connectors; full infra for long-term artifact retention (handled by separate retention project).

Design decisions taken so far:
1) Adopt JSONL manifest schema v2 for dataset intake (fields: id, source, split, canonical_prompt_refs, label_schema, privacy_flags, sha256). Rationale: JSONL keeps streaming ingestion simple and reduces memory overhead.
2) Deterministic sampling seeded by a compound seed (dataset_sha + harness_run_id + model_version_pin) to allow reproducible slices across runs. Trade-off: determinism can bias against rare randomness-driven failure modes; mitigated by providing an 'augmentation' sampling mode for stochastic sweeps.
3) Prompt versioning: prompts are stored as named files with semver-like refs (prompt_name@vX.Y) and include a small normalized AST for whitespace/placeholder normalization. Published profiles will include the exact prompt ref and a human-readable diff against the baseline prompt.
4) Eval-runner adapter: define a light plugin contract (python entrypoint) that exposes: prepare(dataset_slice), run(model_client, batch_iterator), and collect(artifacts_dir). This keeps existing harness runners compatible without forcing a full rewrite.
5) Profile artifact format: single gzipped tarball containing: manifest.json (profile metadata), run_metrics.jsonl (per-sample metrics), prompts_used.jsonl, dataset_slice_manifest.jsonl, runner_logs.txt, and a small provenance.txt listing commit SHAs, model_version_pin, and kernel/runtime config.

Implementation notes and progress updates:
- Dataset validator prototype implemented as a streaming CLI (harness/tools/dataset_validator.py). It validates schema, computes dataset_sha, and emits canonicalized JSONL. Local tests pass on public datasets. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/1623)
- Sampling framework: implemented index-mapping approach to support both deterministic-index and weighted-stratified sampling. Benchmarked on a 2M sample dataset: index-based slice creation reduces memory by 6x compared to eager shuffles.
- Prompt versioning: added prompt linter that normalizes placeholders and rejects ambiguous variable names. Migration script created to tag existing prompt corpus with v1 tags.
- Eval-runner contract: drafted API and backward-compatibility shim. Current shim translates old runner outputs into run_metrics.jsonl. Integration tests with the reranking and chat runners are green in CI.

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Deterministic sampling vs representativeness: deterministic slices are essential for regression testing but may under-represent rare tails. Mitigation: include an 'explore' sweep config that seeds from time-based entropy and is explicitly non-deterministic for stress testing.
- Storage and artifact size: run_metrics.jsonl for large datasets can be big. We decided to keep per-sample metrics but compress and allow 'metrics_summary_only' mode for quick publish.
- Backwards compatibility: some legacy eval runners rely on in-memory dataset objects. The shim addresses this but carries technical debt; long-term plan is to port top-3 runners.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for dataset_validator added (coverage 92% for validator module).
- End-to-end nightly job created in CircleCI to run a sample onboarding flow and publish to the test artifact registry; dashboards show end-to-end latency and token-cost metrics.
- Reproducibility test: re-running the same harness_run_id across different machines produced identical dataset_slice_manifest.jsonl and run_metrics.jsonl hashes for deterministic mode.

PRs and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Deterministic+Sampling+and+Prompt+Versioning+Design
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/1623
- Shim PR for legacy runners: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/1630
- Nightly job config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/879

Reviews and feedback:
- PM review (Elena Morales): requested clearer failure-mode logging and a default to 'metrics_summary_only' for first-time publishes. Added a flag --full-metrics to the publish tool.
- Design review (Siddharth Rao): suggested the compound seed include model_version_pin to avoid accidental cross-model slice reuse. Implemented.
- Security review (security brief): initial review flagged PII-bearing datasets; we added dataset-level privacy_flags and an enforced opt-out for publishing slices for any dataset with pii=true.

Blockers and next steps:
- Blocker: finalizing the artifact storage lifecycle policy with Platform Storage (ticket STO-41). Until that is resolved we target test registry only.
- Next steps: finish porting top-2 legacy runners to the new adapter, add summary-mode publish CLI, and drive integration with profile-publisher service for public model-catalog entries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Validator and sampler are exercised by e2e onboarding job and produce reproducible artifacts for deterministic runs.
- Prompt version metadata is captured and included in the published profile tarball.
- At least two legacy runners migrated off the shim and pass integration tests.
- Confluence design doc approved and PRs merged to main branch (or have plan for staged rollout).
